pre:
You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2021 NSW HSC Business Studies exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 26 [20 marks]: Analyse how a situational analysis (SWOT, product life cycle) may affect marketing strategies.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 20):
17–20 marks: Draws out and clearly relates the implications of a situational analysis (SWOT, PLC) on marketing strategies | Applies relevant case study/studies and contemporary business issues | Presents a sustained, logical and cohesive response and communicates clearly using relevant business terminology and concepts
13–16 marks: Makes evident the relationship between a situational analysis (SWOT, PLC) and marketing strategies | Uses relevant case study/studies and contemporary business issues | Presents a logical and cohesive response using relevant business terminology and concepts
9–12 marks: Provides characteristics and features of a situational analysis (SWOT, PLC) and marketing strategies | Makes reference to case study/studies and/or contemporary business issues | Communicates using relevant business terminology and concepts
5–8 marks: Sketches in general terms a situational analysis and/or marketing strategies | May make reference to case study/studies and/or contemporary business issues | Communicates using some business terminology and concepts
1–4 marks: Makes limited reference to marketing | May identify case study/studies | Uses basic business terminology


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Marketing Process
• situational analysis
– SWOT (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats)
– product life cycle Marketing Strategies
• market segmentation, product/service differentiation and positioning
• products – goods and/or services
– branding
– packaging
• price including pricing methods – cost, market, competition-based
– pricing strategies – skimming, penetration, loss leaders, price points
– price and quality interaction
• promotion
– elements of the promotion mix – advertising, personal selling and relationship marketing, sales promotions, publicity and public relations


WHAT THE REAL MARKERS SAID ABOUT THIS QUESTION:
Better responses: draw out the implications of situational analysis on marketing strategies directly, addressing the key word ‘analyse’
Better responses: use specific information about case study(ies) to help analyse marketing strategies
Better responses: relate the implications of marketing strategies used rather than referring to theory in applying relevant case study information
Better responses: make specific reference to both a SWOT analysis and the product life cycle
Better responses: respond to the question in a logical order, for example, firstly looking at a situational analysis and then working out strategies to use as a consequence
Better responses: provide a variety of links between situational analysis and marketing strategies
Better responses: refer to several specific strategies within the marketing mix.
To improve: using syllabus specific terms regarding marketing strategies consistently throughout the response
To improve: integrating case study information to all parts of question.

STUDENT RESPONSE:
"""
post:
"""

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-20>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '17–20'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a 6 to 8 line plan of what a full-mark response would cover, one line per paragraph, not a full essay>"}
